name: Poco X8s
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 with a 120Hz LTPO OLED is a strong upper-midrange gaming combo — smooth frame rates in demanding titles, though there is no active cooling or dedicated gaming hardware. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Honor Win RT 2
gaming_notes: Flagship gaming hardware: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, active cooling, a 185Hz 2K OLED with 5,000Hz touch sampling and 21ms tap latency, WIN Display/Touch chips and an 800Hz gyroscope. The 12,070mAh battery is the largest ever in a mainstream phone. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Honor Win Turbo 2
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 with a 185Hz 2K OLED and 5,000Hz touch sampling is strong gaming hardware, though it skips the active cooling fan of its pricier siblings. The 12,070mAh battery means marathon sessions. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Honor Play 10
gaming_notes: The Helio G81 with 3-4GB RAM handles casual games and everyday titles at low settings only — this is a basics phone, not a gaming device. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Coolpad Cool X Wide
gaming_notes: The Helio G99 handles casual and mid-tier games acceptably, but the wide low-res LCD and entry positioning make this a media-consumption device, not a gaming phone. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: AGM H6 Pro
gaming_notes: The Unisoc T7250 is an entry-level chip — fine for casual games, not for demanding titles. Rugged durability is the selling point, not performance. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Honor Win 2
gaming_notes: Esports-grade hardware: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, dual active cooling fans with RGB, a 185Hz 2K OLED with 5,000Hz touch sampling, a dedicated WIN Key and X-axis linear motor. The 10,100mAh battery plus 100W wired and 80W wireless charging keep long sessions going. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: OPPO Find X10
gaming_notes: The 3nm Dimensity 9600M with a 144Hz AMOLED and 7,150mAh battery (80W charging) is flagship-class for gaming, though the Find X10 is tuned for cameras first — no dedicated gaming triggers or active cooling. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: OPPO Find X10 Pro Max
gaming_notes: The 2nm Dimensity 9600 Pro with a 144Hz gaming mode, 7,150mAh battery and 80W charging is top-tier silicon, but this is a camera flagship first — no active cooling or gaming triggers. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)

name: Samsung Galaxy F70 5G
gaming_notes: The Exynos 1330 with a 90Hz AMOLED handles casual and mid-weight games fine at medium settings, but it is not a gaming chip — heavy titles need lowered settings and the 25W charging refills the 5,000mAh battery slowly by 2026 standards. (Editorial estimate, not a measured benchmark.)
